why: This is the classic edit distance: dp[i][j] = fewest operations to turn source[:i] into target[:j], and each of insert, delete, replace is one move to a neighbouring cell of the 2-D table.
hints: Look only at the last characters of the two prefixes: either they match, or the last operation was an insert, a delete or a replace.
dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1] if source[i-1] == target[j-1]; otherwise 1 + min(dp[i-1][j-1] (replace), dp[i-1][j] (delete), dp[i][j-1] (insert)).
Base cases dp[i][0] = i and dp[0][j] = j; fill row by row with a rolling array. O(|source|*|target|).
pitfalls: Empty strings: the answer is the other string's length.
Do not add 1 on a match.
statement:
Given two case-sensitive strings source and target, return the minimum number of operations needed to turn source into target. Each operation costs 1 and is one of:

  • insert one character anywhere,
  • delete one character,
  • replace one character with another.

Example: source = "horse", target = "ros".

  1. Replace h with r: horse becomes rorse.
  2. Delete the second r: rorse becomes rose.
  3. Delete e: rose becomes ros.

Two operations are not enough, so the answer is 3. If source is empty, the answer is the length of target (insert everything).
